Chapter 252: The War Begins (6)
Bakel Autonomous Region.
Even though it was night, the moon was nowhere to be seen.
It wasn’t hidden by clouds. It was because of the scorching poison fog formed by the beam fired by the Origin Stone into the civilian residential area during the day.
The boiling poison fog showed no signs of cooling down. The lucky survivors envied those who had died instantly.

Their skin completely melted away, and their softened bones dripped to the ground like mud. Although thousands of people were dying so horribly right near the relief station where Jin stood, not even a scream could be heard. There were no patients left who could scream.
The survivors wandered like ghosts near the relief station, their bodies so battered that they couldn’t even read the sign in front of them.
The war had been a great victory, but far too many innocent lives were lost.
“Five hundred... million...”
Five hundred million, the estimated number of civilians sacrificed by the final strike of the Origin Stone.
Jin stared blankly at the survivors, thinking about that number. It was a figure that felt utterly unreal.
What was worse, the number of victims would only continue to rise. The alliance had already sent every available medical personnel to the affected areas, but it was impossible to treat every patient.

Logically, each individual needed focused treatment from the best healers in the kingdom to survive. However, even if they did survive, they could never return to their former state. At least hundreds of thousands, if not millions, more deaths would be added.
"Sir Jin."
Holy King Lani arrived beside Jin. As soon as Kelliark fled, she had flown here and had been helping the survivors without a moment's rest.
"...Lani."
The two sat in silence for a while, watching outside the tent. Every few seconds, someone collapsed and failed to get back up.
It seemed that even those who had personally been to hell had never seen a more horrific sight.
Yet, amidst such immense suffering and death, an out-of-place golden aura was illuminating the entire affected area.
The power of regeneration.
The power Jin had obtained upon reaching the state of a Genesis Knight was making the ruined land shine.

Jin found the very fact of it even more tormenting. A similar scene had unfolded when the Holy Kingdom was on the verge of destruction from the Demon Realm's invasion, and when the Demon Realm collapsed under Zito's tyranny.
"It’s not your fault. It was Kelliark, that insane monster who did this."
"...I know. But I can't say I bear no responsibility."
His voice was calm.
As Kelliark had said, Jin was struggling to endure the guilt.
He couldn’t afford not to endure. If he broke even once, he would never be able to fight again, or worse, he would fall into demonization.
He said this is just the beginning of the nightmares I will face. He knows my weakness precisely. No, he probably knew it from before. It's just that now, there's nothing holding him back."
Until now, the Zipple had always valued their external reputation.
They had no hesitation in massacring minority groups like the Colon natives for profit, they were at least conscious of the eyes of the 'many'.
But not anymore. Now they no longer need the support of the vast majority of ordinary humans.

"It must mean the Origin Stone is that much closer to completion. And completed Origin Stones already exist in other dimensions. Even if they destroy this world and kill everyone, for them, they can just recreate the world with the Origin Stone."
Grit…!

He gritted his teeth. The bitter taste of blood seeped from between his clenched lips. How could a human do this to another human? How? Such thoughts became inner demons, continuously trying to invade Jin's mind.
Jin stood up from his seat.
"Atonement comes after I've wiped every last one of those bastards from this world. I should go back now... and prepare to fight again. If there is anything you need, feel free to ask, Lani."
"Sir Jin."
"Yes."

"Lady Ayula said that your authority can bring back those who died and turned into light like that. Although, unlike during our Holy Kingdom's time, the Wings of Numerus cannot be added now, eventually, everything will return to its natural order."
Natural Order.

Whenever Jin heard that word, he often thought this. That there was probably no being who had defied the natural order of this world more than himself, a regressor. And that was why he was paying such a heavy price.
But that wasn’t the case anymore.
The atrocities committed by the Zipples, and the unified Zipple, were incomparable to something like regression. Stopping them was a destiny determined from the very beginning, as a regressor.

"...Of course, these words may not be of much comfort. But I, and our companions, believe. That when all the fighting is over, you, Sir Jin, will ultimately make the world shine brighter than before. So please, anytime you need anything, just ask. The Holy Kingdom and I are always ready to do everything for you. I should get back to work as well, as saving the innocent is my mission."
Jin and Lani both left the tent at the same time.

Outside, the alliance's knights, mages, and Elo 2 were busy clearing the poison fog. Even if one wasn't a superhuman who could slice mountains and part seas with a single swing, everyone could fight for the world.
After boarding the Red Owl, Jin immediately looked for Tikan.
""You've returned, my lord..."
"Mm, kid. You're here?"
Jet and his companions greeted Jin, observing him carefully. Up until his brief conversation with Lani in the relief station, Jin had not spoken a single word.
No, it should be said that he couldn’t speak. He had to focus all his mental energy on overcoming his guilt, to the point where he couldn’t even speak a word.
"What happened with Bligiet?"
Bligiet.

After being betrayed by the Zipple, he couldn’t withstand the combined assault of the Genesis Knights and was captured. He had managed to hold out against the three of them for over an hour, but he could not succeed in escaping as he had at the Temple of the Sun God.
"Lady Ameris and Lady Lucy succeeded in restraining him with the help of the Great Patriarch...! I also heard that the separation of your ancestor's body has been completed for now."
"Got it. Check the supplies to be sent to the Holy Kingdom and contact Dino..."
“We’ve already contacted Dino Jaglun, youngest. We told him that all articles from the Hufester press must prioritize consideration for the victims."
“And make sure no unnecessary slander is included just because they lived in Zipple land. We warned that we'd behead anyone who writes such an article."
It was the Tonna brothers. Among them, Daytona stepped forward and briefly hugged Jin.
"Don't try to think of and solve everything by yourself. Focus only on what you and no one else can do. That's why we're here, youngest."
Hearing those words, something welled up inside Jin.
"It’s been a while since you guys felt like my brothers. Thank you for your hard work."
Jin wasn’t the only one feeling guilty.

The companions who had been watching Jin, and his brothers, all felt guilty as well. Even without being a regressor, it was only natural. In that respect, one could say his companions were a little stronger than Jin in that area.
"No word from sister Luna yet?"
Luna was currently leading the fleet in pursuit of the Tower of Tales.
"Yeah. It seems the chase isn't easy. But they say they're getting a lock on its position every now and then, so let's wait a little longer."
Those in pursuit like Luna, those who went to support the relief stations, and those on standby to protect their territories..
Everyone was refining their hatred for the Zipple. Refining it again and again, so that in any situation, they could coldly carve out their hearts and sever their heads.
Soon, Jin made his way to the underground prison of Tikan Palace.
Vahn, Ameiris, and Lucy were monitoring Bligiet in the lowest level of the prison. Bligiet was kneeling, bound in a special restraint made of several different powers.
"You've come, brother Jin."
Vahn, Ameiris, and Lucy all briefly looked at Jin, then exhaled inwardly. They had been worried the entire time, fearing Jin might fall into the abyss of demonization.
"I'm sorry for worrying you all. I know I’m not the only one suffering."
"Don’t say that, Jin."
"Sir Jin..."
Lucy gazed at Jin with a trembling voice.
She was tightly holding the left arm of Temar, which had been separated from Bligiet. It had been a part of the person she loved more than her own life, from a thousand years ago until now.
The left arm, looking no different from when Temar was alive, pierced Luci's heart.

Jin quietly embraced Lucy. In his arms, she finally let out a sobThe one who could not find rest even in death, and the one who had endured solitude for over a thousand years without being able to die. This was all Temar and Lucy's reunion amounted to.
"...I can do anything now. If only I can let Temar rest in peace and stop my daughter."
Lucy’s horn turned red. She activated Bligiet’s restraints.
[Krahh…]
As her horn turned redder, Bligiet suffered more pain. He writhed like a prisoner branded with a hot iron, groaning as he bent his body.
Soon, as the light from her horn faded, Bligiet caught his breath and looked up at Jin and Lucy.
[To inflict pain upon the being who created you... Fuhuhu, this is why the world must be rebuilt.]
"Bligiet, you will never step outside this world again. From now on, you will diligently answer all our questions here, and then you will either be annihilated or sealed."
[Do you think I fear pain? You foolish mortals.]
"You have no reason to be loyal to the Zipples anyway, so wouldn't it be better if we could end this without tiring each other out?"
[Do as you wish. After all, I am…]
Just as Bligiet was about to finish his sentence, Lucy suddenly grabbed his chin forcefully.
The moment Bluggiet said that, Luci suddenly grabbed his jaw forcefully.

"Did you not just hear me? Bligiet. I said I can do anything now. You're not afraid of pain? I, too, was an ego of the Sun God, just like you. That means I know better than anyone what torments you the most... I guarantee, you will regret it if you do not cooperate."
